windguard:
Style: a small illustration for a playing card in a pixel-painterly visual novel set in a stylish Japanese shisha bar at night. Painterly with a subtle pixel grain, soft shading in three or four tones and a clean readable silhouette; not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime line art. Deep night purple (#150d22 to #2e1d45) fills the whole background, with a soft one-directional lavender light (#c9a7e6) from the upper left and a faint warm ember glow from below; warm white (#f6f1fa) only for small highlights, muted gold (#e3bd6e) only as a thin rim accent. Calm, chill, dim indirect lighting, a subtle smoke haze drifting behind the subject. The subject sits exactly centred, fills about 70% of the square frame and reads clearly even when the image is shrunk to 100 pixels; use the same light and finish for every image in this set. Plain background: no table edge, no frame, no border, no vignette ring. No people, no hands, no faces. No shisha pipe, bowl, heat-management device, charcoal block or hose. Square 1024x1024. Never bake in any text, letters, logo, digits, icons or watermark.

SUBJECT (equipment-card exception to the general no-hardware clause above): ONE standalone shisha WINDGUARD, a matte charcoal-purple metal open-bottom cover, upright and centred, a slightly tapered cylinder with a small open top, several simple round ventilation holes near its lower half, a few shallow horizontal ribs near the neck, and ONE thin loop handle on its side. It goes around a bowl and HMD when used but this image shows the empty removed windguard ONLY: NO bowl, HMD, coals, tray, stem, glass base, hose, flame, smoke coming from the object, people or hands. Approximate real height 19 cm; fully visible and readable as a single cover even at 100px. Attached image 1 is a Japanese shop's wind cover photograph for structure only; do not copy the photo background or product finish. Image 2 is an actual Japanese shop hookah photo for relative scale only, do not depict that hookah or its logos. Generic fictional design, deep purple background, no text or logos. Square 1024x1024, opaque illustration, no border. File: windguard.png.

Draw the hookah with correct structure. From top to bottom: a few small cube charcoals (about fingertip size, grey ash with a little red glow, no flames) → a heat management device (HMD), a separate low metal cup sitting on the bowl's rim, holding the coals → the ceramic tobacco bowl (a cup on a slim neck) → a wide ash tray → a vertical stem → a glass base with water only in its lower part. The stem goes straight down into the mouth of the base through a rubber grommet; the base is not an aquarium. Exactly one hose: it starts at the hose port on the side of the stem above the base, sags naturally with gravity, and connects to the base of a rigid handle held in the hand. The hose never forks, breaks, floats, loops around the character, or comes out of the purge valve, bowl, tray or base bottom. In a finished/smoking setup, coals sit inside the HMD, never directly on foil. Use one coherent HMD model; do not mix lids, chimneys or handles from different models. Keep the hookah to real scale: the whole hookah is 60–80 cm tall (on the floor its top reaches a seated person's chest or shoulder). The bowl is a small cup about 6–8 cm tall, with a mouth narrower than an adult's palm; the HMD has the same diameter as the bowl mouth and is only two fingers tall. Bowl + HMD + coals together are only 10–12 cm tall: about 1/6 to 1/7 of the hookah's height and about half the height of the character's face. The tray is about 2.5× the HMD width; coals are fingertip-sized. Do NOT draw an oversized bowl or HMD: the hookah is a modest prop, the character is the subject. Place the hookah at the same depth as the character, with the tray and the upper stem in frame, not in the foreground. Smoke comes from the character's mouth, not from the HMD or hose. If a neck-worn personal mouthpiece is shown, draw a real small mouthpiece body on the chain, not just a chain. Base the hookah and the room on present-day Japanese shisha bars: a slim stainless-steel stem with a wide glass base and a small tray, a silicone bowl with a lotus-type HMD (or another HMD named in the scene), in a Japanese shisha café or bar interior (sofa seating, bright café style or dim indirect lighting). No ornate Middle-Eastern engraved hookah unless asked. Colors and finishes are free; no real brands, logos or text.
This is an isolated accessory card: the general hookah structure above is context for the accessory's correct purpose, not a request to draw a complete hookah or any additional parts. Draw ONLY the named standalone windguard.
